1.1: In the second yeere of King Darius, in the sixt moneth, the first day of the moneth, came ye word of the Lord (by the ministery of the Prophet Haggai) unto Zerubbabel the sonne of Shealtiel, a prince of Judah, and to Jehoshua the sonne of Jehozadak the hie Priest, saying,
1.2: Thus speaketh the Lord of hostes, saying, This people say, The time is not yet come, that the Lords House should be builded.
1.3: Then came the word of the Lord by the ministerie of the Prophet Haggai, saying,
1.4: Is it time for your selves to dwell in your sieled houses, and this House lie waste?
1.5: Now therefore thus saith ye Lord of hostes, Consider your own wayes in your hearts.
1.6: Ye have sowen much, and bring in litle: ye eat, but ye have not ynough: ye drink, but ye are not filled: ye clothe you, but ye be not warm: and he that earneth wages, putteth the wages into a broken bagge.
1.7: Thus sayth the Lord of hostes, Consider your own wayes in your hearts.
1.8: Goe up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build this House, and I wil be fauourable in it, and I will be glorified, sayth the Lord.
1.9: Ye looked for much, and lo, it came to litle: and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. And why, sayth the Lord of hostes? Because of mine House that is waste, and ye runne every man unto his own house.
1.10: Therefore the heaven over you stayed it self from dew, and the earth stayed her fruit.
1.11: And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountaines, and upon the corn, and upon the wine, and upon the oyle, upon all that the ground bringeth foorth: both upon men and upon cattell, and upon all the labour of the hands.
1.12: When Zerubbabel the sonne of Shealtiel, and Jehoshua the sonne of Jehozadak the hie Priest with all the remnant of the people, heard the voyce of the Lord their God, and the wordes of the Prophet Haggai (as the Lord their God had sent him) then the people did fear before the Lord.
1.13: Then spake Haggai the Lords messenger in the Lords message unto the people, saying, I am with you, sayth the Lord.
1.14: And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the sonne of Shealtiel a prince of Judah, and the spirit of Jehoshua the sonne of Jehozadak the hie Priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people, and they came, and did the work in the House of the Lord of hostes their God.

2.1: In the four and twentieth day of the sixt moneth, in the second yeere of King Darius,
2.2: In the seventh moneth, in the one and twentieth day of the moneth, came the word of the Lord by the ministerie of the Prophet Haggai, saying,
2.3: Speak now to Zerubbabel the sonne of Shealtiel prince of Judah, and to Jehoshua the sonne of Jehozadak the hie Priest, and to the residue of the people, saying,
2.4: Who is left among you, that saw this House in her first glory, and how doe you see it now? is it not in your eyes, in comparison of it as nothing?
2.5: Yet now be of good courage, O Zerubbabel, sayth the Lord, and be of good comfort, O Jehoshua, sonne of Jehozadak the hie Priest: and be strong, all ye people of the land, sayth the Lord, and doe it: for I am with you, sayth the Lord of hostes,
2.6: According to the word that I covenanted with you, when ye came out of Egypt: so my Spirit shall remain among you, fear ye not.
2.7: For thus sayth the Lord of hostes, Yet a litle while, and I will shake the heavens and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land:
2.8: And I will move all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come, and I will fill this House with glory, sayth the Lord of hostes.
2.9: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, sayth the Lord of hostes.
2.10: The glory of this last House shall be greater then the first, sayth the Lord of hostes: and in this place will I give peace, sayth the Lord of hostes.
2.11: In the four and twentieth day of the ninth moneth, in the second yeere of Darius, came the word of the Lord unto the Prophet Haggai, saying,
2.12: Thus sayth the Lord of hostes, Ask now the Priests concerning the Law, and say,
2.13: If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt doe touch the bread, or the potage, or the wine, or oyle, or any meat, shall it be holy? And the Priests answered and said, No.
2.14: Then sayde Haggai, If a polluted person touch any of these, shall it be vncleane? And the Priests answered, and sayd, It shalbe vncleane.
2.15: Then answered Haggai, and sayd, So is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the Lord: and so are all the workes of their hands, and that which they offer here, is vncleane.
2.16: And now, I pray you, consider in your mindes: from this day, and afore, even afore a stone was layde upon a stone in the Temple of the Lord:
2.17: Before these things were, when one came to an heap of twentie measures, there were but ten: when one came to the wine press for to draw out fiftie vessels out of the press, there were but twentie.
2.18: I smote you with blasting, and with mildew, and with hail, in all the labours of your hands: yet you turned not to me, saith the Lord.
2.19: Consider, I pray you, in your mindes, from this day, and afore from the four and twentieth day of the ninth moneth, even from the day that the foundation of the Lords Temple was laid: consider it in your mindes.
2.20: Is the seed yet in the barn? as yet the vine, and the figtree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree hath not brought forth: from this day will I bless you.
2.21: And again the word of the Lord came unto Haggai in the four and twentieth day of the moneth, saying,
2.22: Speak to Zerubbabel the prince of Judah, and say, I wil shake the heavens and the earth,
2.23: And I will overthrow the throne of kingdomes, and I wil destroy the strength of the kingdomes of the heathen, and I wil overthrow the charets, and those that ride in them, and the horse and the riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother.
2.24: In that day, saith the Lord of hostes, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel my servant, the sonne of Shealtiel, sayth the Lord, and wil make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, sayth the Lord of hostes.

37:1:1: Because the building of the Temple began to cease, by reason that the people were discouraged by their enemies: and if these two notable men had need to be stirred up and admonished of their duties, what shall we think of other governors, whose doings are either against God, or very cold in his cause?
Who was the son of Histaspis and the third king of the Persians, as some think.
37:1:2: Not that they condemned the building thereof, but they preferred policy and private profit to religion, being content with small beginnings.
37:1:4: Showing that they sought not only their necessities, but their very pleasures before God’s honor.
37:1:6: Consider the plagues of God upon you for preferring your policies to his religion, and because ye seek not him first of all.
37:1:8: That is, my glory shall be set forth by you.
Meaning, that they should leave off their own commodities, and go forward in the building of God’s Temple, and in the setting forth of his religion.
That is, I will hear your prayers according to my promise, 1 Kings 8:21, 29.
37:1:9: And so bring it to nothing.
37:1:12: This declareth that God was the author of the doctrine, and that he was but the minister, as Exod. 14:31; Judg. 7:20; Acts 15:28.
37:1:14: Which declareth that men are inept and dull to serve the Lord, neither can they obey his word or his messengers, before God reform their hearts, and give them new spirits, John 6:44.
37:2:4: For the people according as Isa. 30:19 and Ezek. 41:1, had prophesied, thought this Temple should have been more excellent than Solomon’s Temple, which was destroyed by the Babylonians, but the Prophets meant the spiritual Temple, The Church of Christ.
37:2:5: That is, go forward in building the Temple.
37:2:7: He exhorteth them to patience though see not as yet this Temple so glorious as the Prophets had declared: for this should be accomplished in Christ, by whom all things should be renewed.
37:2:8: Meaning, Christ whom all ought to look for and desire: or by desire he may signify all precious things, as riches, and such like.
37:2:9: Therefore when his time cometh he can make all the treasures of the world to serve his purpose: but the glory of this second Temple doth not stand in material things, neither can be built.
37:2:10: Meaning, all spiritual blessings and felicity purchased by Christ, Phil. 4:7.
37:2:13: That is, the flesh of the sacrifices, whereby he signifieth that thing which of itself is good, cannot make another thing so: and therefore they ought not to justify themselves by their sacrifices and ceremonies: but contrary he that is unclean and not pure of heart, doth corrupt those things and make them detestable unto God, which else are good and godly.
37:2:16: Consider how God did plague you with famine afore you began to build the Temple.
37:2:17: That is, before the building was begun.
37:2:19: From the time they began to build the Temple, he promiseth that God would bless them: and albeit as yet the fruit was not come forth, yet in the gathering they should have plenty.
37:2:20: He exhorteth them to patience, and to abide till the harvest came, and then they should see God’s blessings.
37:2:22: I will make a change, and renew all things in Christ, of whom Zerubbabel here is a figure.
37:2:23: Hereby he showeth that there shall be no let or hindrance, when God will make this wonderful restitution of his Church.
37:2:24: Signifying that his dignity should be most excellent, which thing was accomplished in Christ.
